parsed.why: No visitor-facing legal restriction, but documented hate-speech pattern, physical attacks on a gender-nonconforming figure, and Pride needing 2,000 police against rock-throwing mobs; protections exist yet applied unevenly.

No criminalisation, no entry or facility friction, constitutional protection, civil unions and an openly gay head of state; only gender identity missing from statutes, a resident-facing gap, with violence occasional and unquantified.

Official homophobic statements, recurrent bills to ban transition, a lethal shooting at an LGBT bar, hostile public opinion and no partner recognition; no trans-specific entry or facility ban, but thin recourse and hostile state framing.

Section 379 criminalises cross-dressing itself; security forces documented harassing, detaining, torturing LGBTQI+ people across five years, minister urged arrests, no protections, no NGOs, most LGBTQ citizens fled.

Gender-identity discrimination and hate-crime law, functioning LGBT legal-aid NGO, Pride running annually, official prosecuted for beheading call; offset by inconsistent implementation, politician hate speech and under-reporting to police.
